source_name: НБРСМ — Извештаи за банкарскиот систем на РСМ (banking system reports)
why_relevant: Regulator's quarterly/annual banking-system reports are the canonical series carrying employee headcount, number of business units/branches (експозитури, филијали) and ATMs, per bank and system-wide — the earliest hard evidence of network consolidation and back-office reduction. English versions typically published in parallel.

source_name: НБРСМ — Податоци и показатели за банкарскиот систем (data & indicators)
why_relevant: Structured indicator tables (usually Excel) accompanying the banking-system reports; the machine-readable route to time series on employees and branch counts per bank.

source_name: НБРСМ — Соопштенија / квартални извештаи (press releases)
why_relevant: Regulator press releases announce adoption of each quarterly banking-system report and often summarise structural developments (network, efficiency, staffing) — a low-cost trigger to fetch the underlying report.

source_name: Државен инспекторат за труд (State Labour Inspectorate) — official site
why_relevant: Supervises compliance with labour law; annual work reports, inspection statistics and complaint procedures reveal disputes over redundancies, working-time and dismissal procedures — including at banks — before or instead of media coverage.

source_name: Министерство за економија и труд — страница на ДИТ
why_relevant: Parent-ministry page for the Labour Inspectorate after the 2024 ministry reorganisation; carries mandate, contacts and report links, and resolves which portal currently hosts inspectorate outputs (dit.gov.mk vs mtsp.gov.mk archives).

source_name: МТСП — Закон за инспекцијата на труд и подзаконски акти
why_relevant: Legal baseline for what inspectorate outputs exist and are publishable, and what an employer must do on collective redundancy — needed to interpret disclosure gaps and to frame FOI requests.

source_name: Портал за социјално партнерство / ЕСС документи (МДТ портал)
why_relevant: Government portal hosting social-partnership and collective-agreement documents signed between government, employers and the union confederations — the tripartite layer above bank-level bargaining.

source_name: Стопанска банка АД Скопје — годишен извештај за работењето
why_relevant: Worked example of a bank's own annual operating report carrying employee counts, organisational structure and branch network — the per-bank primary layer to pair with NBRSM aggregates. Same pattern applies to kb.mk, nlb.mk, halkbank.mk, sparkasse.mk.

source_name: Комерцијална банка — Филијали и експозитури (branch directory)
why_relevant: Live branch directories are the cheapest high-frequency proxy for network consolidation: diffing the list month over month detects closures long before any report. Equivalent pages exist for every MK bank.

source_name: НЛБ Банка — соопштенија за јавност (branch/working-hours notices)
why_relevant: Banks announce branch working-hour changes, relocations and closures in their public-notice feed; observed example is an NLB notice on експозитури working hours. These notices are the operational trace of network restructuring.

source_name: МБА — Македонска банкарска асоцијација
why_relevant: Employer-side association of all banks and savings houses (registered 2018, successor to the Chamber's Banking Association). Its presidency and commission rosters are a live map of senior bank executives — leadership moves visible through membership changes — and it is the likely employer counterparty in any sector-level collective bargaining.

source_name: Стопанска комора на Северна Македонија — здруженија (incl. banking/finance)
why_relevant: Chamber associations for banking and non-banking finance host employer positions on labour cost, skills shortages and hiring; historically the home of the banking association. Also an employer-side voice in tripartite wage/collective-agreement debates.

source_name: Државен завод за статистика — пазар на труд / вработени по дејности (NACE K)
why_relevant: Official employment and average-wage series broken down by activity, including K — финансиски дејности и дејности на осигурување. Gives the sector-wide headcount and pay trend against which bank-level cuts are read; also business-demography releases on active entities.

source_name: Open Data Macedonia — Завод за статистика / Пазар на труд / Плати
why_relevant: Third-party mirror of labour-market and wage datasets in machine-readable form; useful fallback when the statistical office's own portal is awkward to scrape. Freshness must be validated against stat.gov.mk.

source_name: ITUC — North Macedonia country page (Survey of violations of trade union rights)
why_relevant: International labour-rights monitoring of North Macedonia; documents bargaining coverage, union-recognition disputes and restructuring conflicts in a comparably framed way, useful for credibility triangulation on union-side claims.

source_name: UNI Europa Finance — sector pages and CEE collective-bargaining work
why_relevant: European federation of finance-sector unions running collective-bargaining strengthening projects in CEE/Western Balkans; its reports and event lists are a pointer to which MK finance union participates and to cross-border bank restructuring (NLB, Sparkasse, OTP groups) affecting MK subsidiaries.

source_name: SeeNews — North Macedonia Company News desk
why_relevant: English-language SEE business wire that files short, dated items specifically on MK bank CEO/management-board/supervisory-board appointments (e.g. 'N. Macedonia's NLB Banka gets new management board chairman', 'Stopanska Banka Skopje to appoint new CEO', 'Sparkasse Bank appoints new board president'). Highest hit-density international source for A5 personnel events in MK banking.

source_name: bne IntelliNews — North Macedonia country desk
why_relevant: English regional desk covering MK banking, ratings actions and fintech/payments market entries; carries executive commentary and named leadership in expansion stories (e.g. Nayax cashless launch in MK), plus sovereign/bank rating coverage that frames governance risk.

source_name: IMF — Republic of North Macedonia Article IV consultations & country reports
why_relevant: Annual Article IV staff reports and concluding statements assess NBRNM supervisory capacity, macroprudential institution-building and financial-sector governance. Recommendations about supervisory resourcing and central-bank capacity are the clearest international read-through on staffing/organisational change at the regulator and, indirectly, at supervised banks.

source_name: IMF/World Bank Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP) — North Macedonia
why_relevant: FSAP assessments (MK: 2003, 2008, 2018 cycle) grade Basel Core Principle compliance including 'fit and proper' licensing of bank directors and senior management, board independence and supervisory staffing adequacy — the international benchmark that dates governance/organisational reforms.

source_name: European Commission — North Macedonia Enlargement Report (annual SWD)
why_relevant: The annual country report's Chapter 9 (financial services), Chapter 4 and public-administration-reform sections judge supervisory institutional capacity, staffing, independence of appointments to regulatory bodies, and BRRD/resolution institution-building — dating structural/organisational change in the MK banking supervision architecture. Also tracks SEPA accession, which drives payments-sector org change.

source_name: Western Balkans InfoHub — mirrored EC enlargement reports
why_relevant: Independent mirror of EC country report PDFs; useful fallback when the EC document-download endpoint rotates URLs, and a way to retain superseded editions for year-on-year diffing.

source_name: EBRD — North Macedonia country strategy, diagnostic and Transition Report
why_relevant: EBRD country strategy 2025-2030, country diagnostic and the annual Transition Report SEE country assessment cover bank ownership structure, foreign-parent dominance, corporate governance of state-owned enterprises and financial-sector institutional quality — context that explains and sometimes names governance/board reform commitments attached to EBRD financing of MK banks.

source_name: Fitch Ratings — North Macedonia sovereign and bank rating actions
why_relevant: Rating action commentaries and Rating Navigator sections explicitly score 'management and strategy' and 'governance', citing management turnover, execution risk and board independence as rating factors for banks; also flag parent-group (NLB, Erste, Halkbank, Steiermärkische) strategy changes that drive MK executive reshuffles.

source_name: Moody's Ratings — issuer pages for MK-relevant banking groups
why_relevant: Credit opinions on parent groups (NLB d.d., Erste Group, Halkbank, Steiermärkische) and on the MK sovereign discuss subsidiary governance and management changes; the 'Governance' pillar of Moody's ESG scoring covers management credibility and board structure.

source_name: S&P Global Market Intelligence — SEE/North Macedonia banking headlines
why_relevant: Publishes short English news items on individual MK banks (e.g. Komercijalna Banka results/strategy), which routinely quote named CEOs and report board decisions; useful for pinning an executive to a role at a specific date.
